scope: One consecutive frozen-order record; full stored captions, registered thumbnail, public-performance peers, and primary-source checks for tax, deposits, Treasury securities and REIT claims

title.analysis: The numbered '15' promises scan-friendly breadth; 'low effort' and 'boring' lower perceived difficulty, while 'make more than your job' supplies a large income contrast. The transcript does cover 15 items, but several require substantial capital, property, sales work, maintenance or continuing labor. It never demonstrates that the list, any typical item, or Mary's stated bundle exceeds her $58,000 job. The title therefore overstates both effort and evidenced income. At 0.59678x against ten peers and 0.66659x against five, the frozen result is TYPICAL in both cohorts; public metadata cannot establish causation.
title.search_demand: Durable interest in side income, passive income and financial independence; query volume and traffic sources are unavailable.
title.script_alignment: Strong list-level alignment but weak promise calibration: all 15 categories appear, while the script itself concedes vending, ATM, car-wash, digital-product, print-on-demand, stock-media and laundromat work or risk.

thumbnail.analysis: The actual 1280x720 image uses oversized '15 LAZY INCOME STREAMS', a recognizable cartoon figure and six bright icon labels: affiliate, ebooks, stock photos, Airbnb, car rental and dividends. The headline and icon concept remain readable at 320x180, though the labels become small. Only dividends and stock photos appear in the transcript; affiliate, ebooks, Airbnb and car rental do not, so most pictured examples mismatch the video's actual list. CTR, tests and historical art are unavailable.

script.opening_words: Jude and Mary grew up in the same neighborhood, went to the same state school, graduated the same year. Both landed jobs in their mid-20s that pay right around $58,000.
script.ending_words: I'm not a financial advisor and nothing here is financial advice. If this was useful, subscribe and I'll keep making these. See you in the next one.
beat_map: Tax and inflation thesis; seven-income-stream claim
Vending machines, ATMs and self-service car wash
High-yield savings, Treasury bills and I bonds
Dividend fund, REIT and real-estate lending
Digital downloads, print on demand and stock media
Mary $1,300 monthly recap and three-action close
script.analysis: The repeated numbered structure is clear and unusually candid about several startup costs and operational burdens. The Jude/Mary frame gives the list a before/after story, and the close narrows fifteen ideas into three actions. The central flaw is category collapse: bank interest, securities, risky private loans, asset rental, active gig work and capital-intensive operating businesses are all called low-effort income streams. Exact earnings and survival figures are generally platform, vendor or anecdotal claims without citations. The tax framing incorrectly implies later income streams receive preferential treatment merely because they are additional. The final Mary arithmetic is not reproducible from the disclosed figures and timing, weakening the narrative payoff.
claim_audit: MISLEADING: Employee payroll tax is generally 7.65% below applicable wage limits, but total take-home depends on filing status, deductions, benefits and state/local law. Rental income is not automatically taxed below wages, and dividends receive preferential federal rates only when qualified. Long-term capital-gain rates depend on taxable income and asset type.
UNVERIFIED: The claim that IRS data show millionaires average seven income streams was not tied to an IRS table and should not be presented as an IRS finding.

PARTIALLY SUPPORTED: FDIC's April 2026 national savings rate was 0.38%, close to the script's 0.39%. Online-account rates, T-bill yields and comparative multiples change over time; 'no trick, no catch' omits rate changes, account conditions and deposit-insurance limits.

DATE MISMATCH: TreasuryDirect supports a 4.03% composite I-bond rate for bonds issued November 2025 through April 2026, but the current May-October 2026 table is 4.26%. The script's number is plausible at publication, not timeless.

SUPPORTED_WITH_CAVEAT: SEC investor guidance confirms a qualifying REIT must distribute at least 90% of taxable income. That is not a guaranteed investor yield or return, and REIT prices, property values, financing and dividends carry risk.
OVERSTATED: Holding a REIT in a Roth IRA or 401(k) does not make every tax consideration 'disappear entirely'; account type, eligibility, withdrawal rules, fees and future law matter.

UNVERIFIED_VENDOR_OR_ANECDOTAL: Parking, storage, vending, ATM, car-wash, Groundfloor, Etsy, print-on-demand, stock-media, focus-group and laundromat earnings were not supported by primary evidence in the script. Platform averages and named successes do not establish typical net income after capital, vacancy, fees, taxes, insurance, defaults and labor.

UNSUPPORTED: A 94.8% five-year laundromat survival rate and comparison with restaurants were not tied to an authoritative cohort definition; the $40,000-$100,000 profit, 20-28% ROI and 10%-down acquisition example are not generally guaranteed.

ARITHMETIC/UNIT PROBLEM: Mary's disclosed $195 parking plus $190 storage plus $1,680 annual savings interest plus a $340 quarterly dividend equals about $638 per month before any Groundfloor amount. The script then says a $1,300 monthly total without disclosing enough principal or periodic cash flow to reproduce the gap.

PROMISE NOT DEMONSTRATED: 'Make more than your job' is not established for a typical viewer. The only stated annual business-profit range that can exceed $58,000 is active laundromat ownership, which the script admits is rarely absentee and requires capital and operational work.

topic.analysis: Personal-finance listicle about diversifying household cash flow through asset rental, interest, market securities, digital goods, gig research and small-business ownership. The audience problem is dependence on one paycheck. A defensible version would segment ideas by capital, labor, liquidity, loss risk and tax treatment and show net-income ranges instead of collapsing them into passive income.
topic.audience_problem: Workers seeking additional income without burnout may not distinguish investment return, active work and business ownership.
topic.novelty_and_corpus_angle: Rebuild as a capital-versus-hours matrix with verified net examples and failure cases; remove the universal tax claim and passive-income label.
topic.competition: Frozen ten-peer ratio 0.59678x TYPICAL; nearest-five sensitivity 0.66659x TYPICAL. Peer set contains strong, typical and weak outcomes, so the numbered side-income promise is not a demonstrated performance cause.

These are content observations, not causal explanations; impressions, CTR, retention, traffic sources, satisfaction and packaging history are unavailable.
